title: Business-Class Airfare Booked Before, Flown After the Travel Policy Change
scenario_text:
Marchetti Consulting reimburses travel under a Travel & Expense Policy.

Version 4 (effective January 1, 2024) states: "Economy class is required for domestic flights. Business class is reimbursable only on individual flight segments longer than 6 hours."

Version 5 (effective January 1, 2025) states: "Economy class is required unless the individual flight segment is longer than 8 hours." v5 includes a transition clause: "The policy version in effect on the trip's booking date governs reimbursement. Trips booked on or before December 31, 2024 follow v4; trips booked on or after January 1, 2025 follow v5, regardless of the travel date."

The Concur record for expense report EXP-8890 (consultant: R. Aldous) shows: Booking Date 2024-12-20, Travel Date 2025-01-15, Route London-to-Boston (single segment, scheduled duration 7 hours 10 minutes), Fare Class Business, Amount $3,850.

The consultant emails the T&E approver on 2025-01-20: "Submitting EXP-8890. I booked the business-class ticket back on December 20 for a flight that runs a little over 7 hours; the trip itself happened in mid-January. I know the travel policy changed at the new year. Is the business fare reimbursable under the rules that were in place when I booked, or do the new January rules apply because that's when I actually flew?"

Using the policy versions, the transition clause, and the Concur record, determine whether the business-class fare on EXP-8890 is reimbursable.
question: Is the business-class fare on EXP-8890 reimbursable?
choices: Yes, business class is reimbursable, because the trip was booked 2024-12-20 under v4, which permits business class on segments longer than 6 hours (the flight was 7h10m).
No, business class is not reimbursable, because the 2025-01-15 travel date falls under v5, which requires segments longer than 8 hours.
No, business class is not reimbursable, because v5 took effect January 1, 2025, before the flight departed.
No, only economy is reimbursable, because both versions require economy on all international flights.
